The scripts turn the shipped data into the numbers, tables and figures of the paper, using the physics in [`fluxpy`](index.md). Each one is run through pixi (for example `pixi run numbers`), or directly with `pixi run python <script>`. The text below is the docstring at the top of each script. The sequence of the steps is described under [Reproduction](../reproduce.md).

## Eddy-covariance reference

(scripts/run_ec_aggregation.py)=
### `scripts/run_ec_aggregation.py`

**Run:** `pixi run ec-segments`  ·  [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/FranzFlink/bacsam2-flux-analysis/blob/main/scripts/run_ec_aggregation.py)

100 Hz T-Bird data  ->  the 5 km EC segment file (manuscript Sect. 2.1 and 3.1).

Reads

```text
data/observations/processed/t-bird_unified/noseboom_unified.nc    100 Hz T-Bird
data/observations/processed/polar6_unified/radiation_unified.nc  20 Hz KT-19 surface temperature
data/observations/processed/satellite_unified/sic_*.nc           sea-ice concentration
data/observations/ar/analysis_ready_polar6_legs_metadata.csv     start/end time of every leg
```

Writes

```text
data/observations/ar/analysis_ready_polar6_turbulent_fluxes_latest_5km.nc
```

The physics is in [`fluxpy.aggregate`](fluxpy.aggregate.md) (segments), [`fluxpy.eddy_covariance`](fluxpy.eddy_covariance.md) (flux and
random error) and [`fluxpy.qc`](fluxpy.qc.md) (integrity check); this script only loads the files.

Run:  pixi run ec-segments            (about 30 s)

```text
pixi run verify-ec              recomputes into a temporary file and compares
```

(scripts/verify_ec_reproduction.py)=
### `scripts/verify_ec_reproduction.py`

**Run:** `pixi run verify-ec`  ·  [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/FranzFlink/bacsam2-flux-analysis/blob/main/scripts/verify_ec_reproduction.py)

Recompute the eddy-covariance segment fluxes from the shipped 100 Hz T-Bird
data into a temporary file and compare them with the shipped segment file.

Shows that the EC flux, its random error and the integrity check of every
shipped segment follow from the 100 Hz data and the code in this repository,
on your machine.

Run:  pixi run verify-ec

(scripts/ec_segment_placement.py)=
### `scripts/ec_segment_placement.py`

**Run:** `pixi run placement`  ·  [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/FranzFlink/bacsam2-flux-analysis/blob/main/scripts/ec_segment_placement.py)

Segment-placement uncertainty of the EC sensible heat flux.

Where exactly a 5 km segment is cut out of a flight leg is arbitrary. To
quantify what this choice does to the flux, a 5 km window is moved through
every low-level leg in 0.05 km steps and the EC flux is computed at each
position (same estimator as the segment fluxes: linear detrend, cospectrum
integrated over 0.1-20 Hz). For each analysis segment, the placement
uncertainty is the standard deviation of all window fluxes that overlap the
segment, weighted by their fractional overlap (triangular weights).

Output: data/observations/ar/ec_segment_placement.nc
Run:    pixi run placement      (about 2 minutes)

(scripts/ec_window_length.py)=
### `scripts/ec_window_length.py`

**Run:** `pixi run window-length`  ·  [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/FranzFlink/bacsam2-flux-analysis/blob/main/scripts/ec_window_length.py)

EC window-length experiment (manuscript Fig. 3).

Each low-level T-Bird leg is cut into consecutive sub-windows of length L
(0.5 ... 50 km). For every L the EC flux of the sub-windows is compared with
the EC flux of the complete leg; the random error of the sub-window fluxes and
the shares of sub-windows whose flux exceeds 1, 2 and 3 times its random error are collected. Same estimator as the
segment fluxes (linear detrend, cospectrum integrated over 0.1-20 Hz).

Output: data/observations/ar/ec_leg_length_sensitivity/ec_sensitivity_summary.csv
Run:    pixi run window-length      (about 2 minutes)

## Bulk fluxes, numbers and tables

(scripts/calc_bulk_and_ec_fluxes.py)=
### `scripts/calc_bulk_and_ec_fluxes.py`

**Run:** `pixi run precompute`  ·  [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/FranzFlink/bacsam2-flux-analysis/blob/main/scripts/calc_bulk_and_ec_fluxes.py)

Bulk fluxes for every forcing, the sensitivity sweep and the input perturbations.

Manuscript: Sect. 3.2 (bulk method), Sect. 4.1 (comparison, Table 4, Figs. 4-6),
Sect. 4.2 (sensitivity, Table 3, Fig. 7), Table 2 (uncertainty budget), Appendix C.

Writes

```text
data/model_output/sensitivity_figure_data.nc      every flux estimate on the 90 segments
data/model_output/sensitivity_summary_table.csv   skill of every configuration
```

Stages

```text
1  load_obs             the 90 low-level segments over sea ice with the EC reference
2  along-track inputs   MODIS IST, ERA5 level 136 (T, wind, height), ERA5 skin temperature,
                        surface pressure and surface flux, CARRA surface flux, at each segment.
                        Cached in along_track_inputs.nc so that the bulk computation
                        runs without the gridded files (pixi run verify-cache re-extracts).
3  sensitivity sweep    every configuration of Table C1, once with the ERA5-MODIS forcing
                        (sweep A) and once with the ERA5-only forcing (sweep B); the in-situ
                        estimate is part of every run
4  input perturbations  the reference configuration with T_s, T_air and U shifted by fixed
                        amounts, for the uncertainty budget and the input sensitivities
5  output
```

All physics comes from fluxpy (bulk, stability, sensitivity). The model-diagnosed
fluxes of ERA5 and CARRA are positive downward in the products and are sign-flipped
here, once, so that every H_* is positive upward.

Run:  pixi run precompute                       (about 15 s with the cache)

```text
python scripts/calc_bulk_and_ec_fluxes.py --extract-only   (raw-data host: rebuild the cache)
```

(scripts/verify_along_track_cache.py)=
### `scripts/verify_along_track_cache.py`

**Run:** `pixi run verify-cache`  ·  [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/FranzFlink/bacsam2-flux-analysis/blob/main/scripts/verify_along_track_cache.py)

Re-extract the MODIS and ERA5 values at the 90 segments from the shipped gridded
files and compare them with the shipped along-track file (along_track_inputs.nc).

The CARRA surface flux in that file cannot be re-extracted here, because the CARRA
forecast file is not part of the repository.

Run:  pixi run verify-cache

(scripts/manuscript_numbers.py)=
### `scripts/manuscript_numbers.py`

**Run:** `pixi run numbers`  ·  [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/FranzFlink/bacsam2-flux-analysis/blob/main/scripts/manuscript_numbers.py)

Every number quoted in the manuscript text and in Table 4, printed from the pipeline output.

Single source of truth for the printed statistics. Run after any pipeline change
and copy the numbers from here, never from an older PDF, a notebook or git
history. `pixi run check` compares this output with `expected_numbers.txt`.

Precision, as printed in the paper: statistics (slopes and their intervals,
correlations, biases, errors and uncertainties, sensitivities) with two decimals;
flux values, temperatures, Ri_b and flight facts with one; counts and percentages
as integers.

Blocks (in the order printed) and where they appear in the manuscript

```text
EC reference ........................ Sect. 3.1, Appendix A2 (n, integrity check, random error, 1/2/3 sigma)
reference configuration ............. Table 4, Sect. 4.1 (slope, r, r2, within-leg r, bias, RMSE, CI)
amplitude-matched configuration ..... Table 4, Sect. 4.2 (alpha_T = 1e-4)
alpha_T sweep ....................... Sect. 4.2, Fig. 7, Table C1
satellite T_s benefit ............... Sect. 4.1, Discussion (heterogeneous vs homogeneous half)
alpha_T is a weak knob .............. Discussion
window-length experiment ............ Sect. 3.1, Fig. 3
uncertainty budget .................. Table 2
further numbers ..................... input sensitivities (Sect. 4.2), CARRA subset (Sect. 4.1), paired bootstrap
sample and flight facts ............. abstract, Sect. 2.1, 3.1, 4 (heights, airspeed, latitude, flux extremes)
percentages ......................... abstract, Sect. 4.1, Discussion, Conclusions (amplitude, variance, reduction)
Richardson number ................... Appendix B1 (range of Ri_b, effect of a bound)
```

Framework (Sect. 4.1): amplitude skill is a regression slope and variability skill
a correlation, because RMSE in this low-flux regime rewards estimates that shrink
towards zero. The reference configuration uses the conventional alpha_T = 1e-1;
the amplitude-matched alpha_T = 1e-4 is reported alongside.

Run:  pixi run numbers

(scripts/ec_quality.py)=
### `scripts/ec_quality.py`

**Run:** `pixi run ec-quality`  ·  [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/FranzFlink/bacsam2-flux-analysis/blob/main/scripts/ec_quality.py)

Quality of the EC reference: every number of manuscript Appendix A.

Sections (numbered as printed)

```text
1  Why ratio-type quality criteria are not used to discard segments: they respond to
   the size of the flux, not to the quality of the measurement (Appendix A3).
2  Robustness: slope and correlation of four estimates under eight alternative
   screenings (Table A1, written to tables_manuscript/table_qc_robustness.tex).
3  Random error: Finkelstein-Sims against surrogate data (which contain only the
   first term of the sum and are expected to be lower; Rannik et al., 2016) and
   against the segment-placement spread; sensitivity to the lag range; the factor
   missing from the shortcut form of the Lenschow et al. (1994) error (Appendix A2).
4  Physical consistency: the direction of the measured flux against the measured
   temperature difference, without any transfer coefficient (Appendix A4).
5  The pitch resonance of the towed T-Bird near 1 Hz: an upper bound of its effect
   on the fluxes and on the comparison (Appendix A4).
```

Run:  pixi run ec-quality      (about 1 minute; needs pixi run precompute)

(scripts/robustness_checks.py)=
### `scripts/robustness_checks.py`

**Run:** `pixi run robustness`  ·  [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/FranzFlink/bacsam2-flux-analysis/blob/main/scripts/robustness_checks.py)

Robustness of the comparison, printed from the pipeline output.

The checks test the statements of the manuscript against the choice of metric, errors
in the reference, the dependence between neighbouring segments, the cloud cover of the
satellite retrieval, the stability correction, the fitting of alpha_T and the
measurement height. `pixi run check` compares this output with
`expected_numbers.txt` like every other number.

Blocks (in the order printed) and what each one tests

```text
1  more metrics ...................... the OLS slope is r times the ratio of standard deviations;
                                       intercept, sd ratio, mean absolute error, and what a
                                       zero-flux or constant forecast would score
2  errors in the reference ........... how much the random error of the EC flux flattens
                                       the regression slopes (regression dilution)
3  dependent segments ................ segments along a leg are not independent: confidence
                                       intervals with blocks of segments and legs as units,
                                       leave-one-day-out, the satellite gain under both
4  satellite surface temperature ..... how many segments have a genuine MODIS value, the
                                       comparison on those only, T_s of MODIS / ERA5 vs KT-19
5  stability ......................... sampled Ri_b, the stability factor f_h = C_h / C_h,n,
                                       and the per-segment spread of the eight schemes
6  alpha_T on withheld days .......... amplitude matching fitted on three days, tested on the fourth
7  measurement height ................ lower half vs upper half of the T-Bird heights
```

Run:  pixi run robustness      (needs pixi run precompute; about 10 s)

(scripts/ec_band_sensitivity.py)=
### `scripts/ec_band_sensitivity.py`

**Run:** `pixi run ec-bands`  ·  [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/FranzFlink/bacsam2-flux-analysis/blob/main/scripts/ec_band_sensitivity.py)

Sensitivity of the EC reference and of the comparison to the frequency band of the flux.

Manuscript Sect. 3.1 integrates the w-theta cospectrum over 0.1-20 Hz. The window-length
experiment (Fig. 3) tests the consistency of that choice but not how much flux lies outside
the band. Here every EC flux is recomputed from the 100 Hz data with other bands, and the
comparison (slope b / correlation r of the three bulk estimates against the EC flux) is
repeated with each of them. The first row reproduces the shipped EC fluxes.

A 5 km segment lasts about 83 s, so its lowest resolved frequency is about 0.012 Hz;
bands that start below 0.05 Hz rest on one or two cycles and are not used.

Run:  pixi run ec-bands      (about 30 s)

(scripts/make_manuscript_tables.py)=
### `scripts/make_manuscript_tables.py`

**Run:** `pixi run tables`  ·  [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/FranzFlink/bacsam2-flux-analysis/blob/main/scripts/make_manuscript_tables.py)

The data-derived table bodies of the manuscript, written to tables_manuscript/.

```text
table_sensitivity_summary.tex   Table 3  (Sect. 4.2): range of slope and r over each sensitivity axis
table_sensitivity_full.tex      Table C1 (Appendix C): every configuration, slope and r of both pathways
table_uncertainty_budget.tex    Table 2  (Sect. 3.2): flux-uncertainty budget
```

The bodies are pasted into manuscript.tex, so the printed tables cannot drift
from the analysis. (Table A1 is written by scripts/ec_quality.py.)

Run:  pixi run tables

(scripts/check_expected_numbers.py)=
### `scripts/check_expected_numbers.py`

**Run:** `pixi run check`  ·  [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/FranzFlink/bacsam2-flux-analysis/blob/main/scripts/check_expected_numbers.py)

Compare the numbers printed by the number scripts with expected_numbers.txt.

expected_numbers.txt is the committed output of manuscript_numbers.py (text and
Table 4), ec_quality.py (Appendix A), robustness_checks.py and
ec_band_sensitivity.py (robustness of the comparison) for this version
of the repository. Numbers are compared with a tolerance of 0.02 (two
units in the last digit of a two-decimal statistic) so that harmless
floating-point differences between operating systems do not raise a false alarm.

Run:  pixi run check
Update the reference after an intended change:

```text
pixi run python scripts/check_expected_numbers.py --update
```

## Figures

(figures_manuscript/fig01_campaign_overview.py)=
### `figures_manuscript/fig01_campaign_overview.py`

**Run:** `pixi run python figures_manuscript/fig01_campaign_overview.py`  ·  [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/FranzFlink/bacsam2-flux-analysis/blob/main/figures_manuscript/fig01_campaign_overview.py)

Fig. 1 -- campaign overview map (manuscript Sect. 2.1, fig:campaign_overview).

April-2024 mean sea-ice concentration (merged MODIS-AMSR2, 1 km) with all 13
Polar 6 master tracks of BACSAM-II (PANGAEA, doi:10.1594/PANGAEA.971763).
The four analysed low-level flight days are highlighted in the batlow day
colours (17 April in red, drawn on top) and their focus regions (the detail panels of the low-level flight
figure) are drawn as labelled rectangles.  A flight is coloured only if it
overlaps in time with the analysed 5-km segments (three flights flew on
13 April; only the one containing the low-level legs is highlighted).

Run:  pixi run python figures_manuscript/fig01_campaign_overview.py

(figures_manuscript/fig02_meteo_overview.py)=
### `figures_manuscript/fig02_meteo_overview.py`

**Run:** `pixi run python figures_manuscript/fig02_meteo_overview.py`  ·  [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/FranzFlink/bacsam2-flux-analysis/blob/main/figures_manuscript/fig02_meteo_overview.py)

Fig. 2 (fig:bulk_methods_overview) -- thermodynamic inputs of the bulk flux estimates (manuscript Sect. 2.3).

For the 90 segments of the four low-level flight days:

* **(a)** pseudo profiles of potential temperature per flight day: the surface value
  theta_s and theta_air at the T-Bird (~24 m) and Polar 6 (~70 m) levels for the
  observations, and the corresponding levels of ERA5 (with ERA5 or MODIS T_s) and
  CARRA; thin lines are single segments, thick lines the daily median;
* **(b)** distributions of the surface temperature T_s of the four sources;
* **(c)** distributions of the near-surface stratification, theta at ~30 m minus theta_s.

Inputs (all shipped): the segment file (KT-19 T_s, T-Bird T, p, height), the Polar 6
aircraft-level side file, MODIS IST, ERA5 model levels 134-137 and single levels,
CARRA surface and 30 / 75 m height levels. MODIS and ERA5 are colocated with the
same functions as the bulk fluxes (scripts/calc_bulk_and_ec_fluxes.py); the
potential temperature is [`fluxpy.util.potential_temperature`](#fluxpy.util.potential_temperature) with the pressure of
each level.

Run:  pixi run python figures_manuscript/fig02_meteo_overview.py

(figures_manuscript/fig06_flux_scatter.py)=
### `figures_manuscript/fig06_flux_scatter.py`

**Run:** `pixi run python figures_manuscript/fig06_flux_scatter.py`  ·  [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/FranzFlink/bacsam2-flux-analysis/blob/main/figures_manuscript/fig06_flux_scatter.py)

Fig. 6 (fig:flux_scatter_comparison) -- bulk vs EC, 2x2 (manuscript Sect. 4.1).

* **(a)** H_S,obs,bulk against H_S,obs,EC;
* **(b)** histograms of the EC, T-Bird bulk and ERA5-MODIS bulk fluxes;
* **(c)** H_S,RS,bulk against H_S,obs,EC;
* **(d)** histograms of the EC flux and the reanalysis-driven estimates.

Scatter points are coloured by the bulk Richardson number; the error bars are the
1-sigma uncertainties of Table 2 ([`fluxpy.uncertainty`](fluxpy.uncertainty.md)). The regression slope b,
correlation r and bias are printed for the caption. All fluxes are positive
upward; the model-diagnosed fluxes are already stored with this sign.

Run:  pixi run python figures_manuscript/fig06_flux_scatter.py

(figures_manuscript/fig07_sensitivity.py)=
### `figures_manuscript/fig07_sensitivity.py`

**Run:** `pixi run python figures_manuscript/fig07_sensitivity.py`  ·  [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/FranzFlink/bacsam2-flux-analysis/blob/main/figures_manuscript/fig07_sensitivity.py)

Fig. 7 (fig:sensitivity_summary) — sensitivity in the slope/r framework (manuscript Sect. 4.2).

Tornado-chart layout: three shared-y panels, (a) regression slope b on the EC
reference (ideal 1), (b) correlation r, (c) bias (ideal 0). Each configuration
row shows the three offline bulk estimates as dots (T-Bird green, ERA5-MODIS
orange, ERA5-only blue; no connector line); the model-diagnosed
ERA5/CARRA fluxes are the dashed vertical benchmark lines. Representative
configurations only (full matrix: Table C1).

Data: obs_*/rs_* metrics from sensitivity_summary_table.csv; the ERA5-only
bulk is the rs_* pathway of the matching '<label>_era5only' run; diag metrics
are computed from sensitivity_figure_data.nc against the EC reference.

Run:  pixi run python figures_manuscript/fig07_sensitivity.py

(figures_manuscript/figA1_spectral_qc.py)=
### `figures_manuscript/figA1_spectral_qc.py`

**Run:** `pixi run python figures_manuscript/figA1_spectral_qc.py`  ·  [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/FranzFlink/bacsam2-flux-analysis/blob/main/figures_manuscript/figA1_spectral_qc.py)

Figure A1 -- spectral diagnostics of the EC segments (fig:spectral_qc).

One line per 5-km T-Bird segment of the four low-level flight days, coloured
by whether the segment's flux exceeds twice its random error; black line = median over the plotted segments.

* **(a-d)** power spectra of theta, w, u, v with -5/3 guides;
* **(e)** frequency-weighted cospectrum f*C_wtheta;
* **(f)** normalised ogive O_wtheta (fluxes above twice their random error only:
  the normalisation by the total covariance is meaningless for a flux
  that cannot be distinguished from zero).

## Documentation

(book/build_book.py)=
### `book/build_book.py`

**Run:** `pixi run book`  ·  [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/FranzFlink/bacsam2-flux-analysis/blob/main/book/build_book.py)

Build and execute the notebooks of the didactic book.

The notebooks follow the structure of the manuscript and recompute its central
numbers from the shipped data, using the same `fluxpy` functions
as the pipeline. They are generated from the cell lists below and executed, so
every figure and number in them is produced on your machine.

Run:  pixi run book        (about 2 minutes; run `pixi run precompute` first)

(paper/export_clean_manuscript.py)=
### `paper/export_clean_manuscript.py`

**Run:** `pixi run paper`  ·  [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/FranzFlink/bacsam2-flux-analysis/blob/main/paper/export_clean_manuscript.py)

Write a clean, self-contained copy of the manuscript, annotated with the code behind each part.

The authoritative manuscript is a Copernicus LaTeX file that lives outside this
repository. This script turns it into `paper/manuscript_clean.tex`:

* every `%` comment (co-author notes, revision history, template text) removed,
  and the class boilerplate (preamble, template placeholders "TEXT") dropped;
* `\ref` / `\eqref` replaced by the printed numbers and `\citet` / `\citep`
  by "Author et al. (Year)", both taken from the compiled `.aux` and `.bbl`,
  so the text reads like the PDF;
* `% [code]` annotations added after every section, equation, figure and table
  label that name the module, script or file in this repository that implements
  or produces it (the map is `CODE_MAP` below);
* figures point at their PNG in `figures_manuscript/output/`.

The copy is for reading, not for compiling. It is a snapshot: the header records
the source file and its git state.

Run:  pixi run paper      (needs the manuscript folder next to this repository;

```text
python paper/export_clean_manuscript.py --tex PATH/manuscript.tex  otherwise)
```

(docs/build_api.py)=
### `docs/build_api.py`

**Run:** `pixi run api`  ·  [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/FranzFlink/bacsam2-flux-analysis/blob/main/docs/build_api.py)

Write the API reference (`docs/api/`) and the figure pages (`docs/figures/`) of the website.

MyST, the engine of the website, has no autodoc. This script does what Sphinx's
autodoc and autosummary do for a Sphinx site:

* one page per `fluxpy` module, in the order of the module map in
  `fluxpy/__init__.py` (paper order): the module docstring, a summary table, every
  public constant (value and the `#:` comment of its definition), class (fields with
  type, default and meaning) and function (signature, parameter table with types and
  defaults, docstring), each with a link to the source on GitHub and the source itself;
* one page on every script (`scripts/`, `figures_manuscript/`, the book, paper and
  website builders): its docstring and the pixi task that runs it;
* an index page;
* one page per manuscript figure (`docs/figures/`): the figure, its caption from the
  reading copy of the manuscript (`paper/manuscript_clean.tex`), the docstring of its
  script, the fluxpy objects it uses, and the script itself.

Docstrings are plain text with a little reStructuredText (`code``, `:func:``
roles, underlined headings, numpydoc `Parameters` sections, simple tables, `::`
literal blocks) and `$...$` math; they are translated to MyST markdown here, and
every name that is documented becomes a link.

The pages are committed like the executed book chapters, so the website build needs
neither the data nor the analysis environment. `tests/test_api_docs.py` fails when a
docstring or signature changed and the pages were not rebuilt.

Run:  pixi run api
